verdict.summary: I read the abstracts of 8 candidates. The Cu-N3 motif on carbon counts as reported experimentally. Two papers state Cu-N3 outright. In 10.1016/j.jcis.2023.05.100 the Cu-N3-C sites on carbon nanosheets are proved by EXAFS. In 10.1021/prechem.5c00420 single Cu atoms in N-doped porous carbon have a Cu-N3 coordination. In 10.1021/jacs.1c03788 the Cu starts as Cu-N4 and operando XAS shows it becoming Cu+-N3 under ORR conditions. That makes it a looser match, because N3 appears only as a potential-driven working state. Four papers are related only. 10.1016/j.jmgm.2020.107537 and 10.1039/d4cp03779k are DFT-only studies of CuN3 in graphene (ORR/OER, not HER). 10.1021/acsomega.2c01562 is a computed 2D C3N3Cu sheet, and the two carbon-nitride papers (10.1021/acsami.1c17782 and 10.1038/s41467-026-73151-8) use Cu-N3 on a carbon nitride support. I did not open the Cu-S1N3 (N3 plus an S donor) or Cu-N4-C (four N) papers, because their donor sets differ and they are related at most. Cu-N3 sites on carbon are therefore not new. None of these abstracts reports hydrogen evolution or dG_H on Cu-N3, so the HER data for the graphene single-vacancy model (dG_H = +0.18 eV) may still be new. The abstracts do not show whether the experimental N3 sites sit in a graphene single vacancy. This is a draft and needs expert checking.

closest.title: Unraveling the Origin of Sulfur-Doped Fe-N-C Single-Atom Catalyst for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Activity: Effect of Iron Spin-State Tuning
closest.coordination: C-FeN4-S moiety, with S in the second coordination sphere of Fe-N-C

verdict.summary: I opened the abstracts of 8 candidates and ran one extra targeted semantic search. None describes a single Fe atom with an S2C2 first shell (two S, two C) on carbon. The closest papers use other donor sets. FeNnS4-n and FeSxN4-x on graphene are DFT studies with N and S donors. TM-S4 on graphene lists other metals in its abstract. The Fe-NSC and S-doped Fe-N-C papers have Fe-N4 first shells with S in the periphery or second sphere. The Fe1/NC HER paper is Fe-Nx only. Axial S on FeN4 is not S2C2 either. The extra search returned no S2C2 hit. Only abstracts and titles were checked, not full texts or SI, so a paper that mentions S2C2 only in its main text could be missed. This is a draft and needs your own check. The motif looks unreported, with related work only.

counter_evidence.title: Enhanced Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction Reactivity of S- and N-Doped Fe-Embedded Graphene
counter_evidence.why: Related only. Abstract covers Fe-N(n)S(4-n) (n=1-4) in graphene. These are N and S donors and no C donors, so there is no Fe-S2C2. FeN2S2 is the closest, but it has a different donor set.

counter_evidence.title: Sulfur-Coordinated Transition Metal Atom in Graphene for Electrocatalytic Nitrogen Reduction with an Electronic Descriptor
counter_evidence.why: Related only. Abstract describes TM-S4 on graphene for 25 transition metals, with an S4 first shell. It does not describe S2C2 and does not name Fe as a highlighted case.

counter_evidence.title: Stability of graphene-based single-atom catalysts across the first-row transition series: the interplay of coordination, composition, and metal identity
counter_evidence.why: Related only. Abstract covers first-row metals on mono- and divacancy graphene, with and without N doping. It does not mention S, so no S2C2 donor set.

challenge.notes: Not refuted. I ran 5 new semantic searches (of the 8 allowed) and opened 3 abstracts (of the 4 allowed). The searches covered Fe-N/S co-doped graphene with S2C2, Fe1S2C2 with EXAFS, Fe-S coordination without N, MS2C2 double vacancy DFT, and Fe/S-doped graphene HER dG_H. No abstract states a single Fe atom with two S and two C donors on carbon. The other hits were Fe-N4 with peripheral or second-shell S (Fe-N-C, S-doped Fe-N-C), Fe-N3S, Fe-NS dual-doped carbon, S-bridged dual-Fe or Fe2S2 clusters, and Co-S/N-C for HER. All of these are related only. Limitation: only titles and abstracts were checked, so a paper that gives S2C2 only in its main text or SI could still be missed. The verdict stays related_only, and this is a draft for your own check.
